headword: {少年時代|しょうねんじだい}

definitions.explanation: The period of a person's life from later childhood into the early teens, looked back on as a stage. Strictly it refers to a boy's youth, but it is also used loosely for childhood in general, especially in reminiscence and biography.

examples.japanese: {少年時代|しょうねんじだい}を{思|おも}い{出|だ}す。
{父|ちち}は{少年時代|しょうねんじだい}を{北海道|ほっかいどう}で{過|す}ごした。
examples.english: My father spent his boyhood in Hokkaido.

examples.japanese: {少年時代|しょうねんじだい}に{読|よ}んだ{一冊|いっさつ}の{本|ほん}が、その{後|ご}の{人生|じんせい}を{決|き}めたと{語|かた}っている。
examples.english: He says that a single book he read in boyhood determined the rest of his life.

notes:
{少年|しょうねん} (boy, youth) + {時代|じだい} (era, period of life). The pattern noun + {時代|じだい} is productive for life stages: {学生|がくせい}{時代|じだい} (student days), {子供|こども}{時代|じだい} (childhood).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {少年時代|しょうねんじだい}を{過|す}ごす: to spend one's boyhood (somewhere)
- {少年時代|しょうねんじだい}を{振|ふ}り{返|かえ}る: to look back on one's boyhood
- {少年時代|しょうねんじだい}の{思|おも}い{出|で}: memories of boyhood

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {少女|しょうじょ}{時代|じだい}: girlhood — the female counterpart
- {幼少|ようしょう}{期|き}: early childhood — more formal, and covers younger years
